Merge this into the existing `_test_products` e2e instead of adding a second copy.
'converts query runtime failures to bad request' no longer exercises the user-query failure path — the mock now throws on the new `SET TimeZone` statement
~50-row hard-coded matrix of Postgres built-in OIDs is broader scope than the date/time change under review and is version-brittle
`create` and `update` return the datasource row including the encrypted password blob, unlike `findOne`/`findAllByWorkspace` which mask it
Unit-spec pg mock doesn't model the new SET statements, so the SET TimeZone/DateStyle calls return a full fake result set
Assertions weakened by `String(...)` coercion, hiding the actual value type the parser change affects
The `statement_timeout` guard may be neutralised from inside the submitted SELECT via `set_config`, enabling long-running query DoS
`toCell` is a generic value→string serializer exported from a store module and now consumed by the backend test; layer/placement is questionable
Unit-test mock not updated for the new session-setup statements: the runtime-failure test now throws on `SET TimeZone`, so it no longer exercises the wrapped-query failure path
Query-execution behavior change (session TimeZone/DateStyle + raw-text date parsers) is not recorded in the canonical datasource design doc
Forcing `SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'` also changes date *input* interpretation and can silently produce wrong results for user queries written against a DMY server

Read-only enforcement is a SQL keyword blocklist only; the newly added session `SET` block omits `default_transaction_read_only`, so side-effecting functions inside a SELECT can still write to the connected database
Datasource TLS connections disable certificate verification (`rejectUnauthorized: false`), so a network attacker can MITM and capture the decrypted datasource credentials

SSRF: fully user-controlled `host`/`port` are dialed by the server and connection errors are reflected verbatim, allowing internal port/service probing and unix-socket access to the app's own database

Custom parser only covers scalar DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ OIDs, so array/range/composite columns of the same types still reach ReadOnlyStore as JS Dates, producing a different cell rendering than scalars
RAW_TEXT_OIDS only covers scalar DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ; array and range date/time types still get parsed into JS `Date` and remain timezone-shifted
The `MONEY` assertion is locale-dependent and may fail on non-US clusters.
No test pins the stated motivation: results should not shift with the Node runtime timezone
Three sequential round-trips per query for session setup where one statement (or a connection `options` string) would do

Design docs still describe the old contract: query execution says nothing about the UTC/DateStyle session settings or raw-text date values, and the ReadOnlyStore section still describes plain stringification
Newly exported `toCell` turns nullish input into the literal strings 'null'/'undefined'; the null guard lives only in its one internal caller
New exported `toCell` helper has no test in packages/sheets; its `Date` branch is untested anywhere

New design doc deviates from docs/design/template.md heading structure

Test claims 'missing or unparseable' issuedAt but only exercises the missing case
Guard distinguishes "secret not configured" (503) from "bad signature" (401) to unauthenticated callers, leaking backend configuration state

List ordering has no final unique tiebreak, so documents sharing an identical `updatedAt`/`createdAt` (e.g. all rows right after the backfill migration) come back in an unspecified, potentially varying Postgres order

Mass assignment into the `DocumentService.updateDocument` sink touched by this diff: the v1 API PATCH forwards the raw request body as the Prisma update payload, allowing arbitrary scalar columns (`workspaceId`, `authorID`, `fileId`) to be set
Raw-body capture wiring (path-scoped `verify` hook) is never exercised; the guard spec injects `rawBody` by hand, so a wrong path constant would ship green
`updateDocument`'s new "bump only when data is non-empty" heuristic counts keys, not defined values, so an all-`undefined` update body still bumps `updatedAt`
Public REST API v1 document list neither orders by nor documents the new `updatedAt` field

`YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` env documentation not updated for its new, harder requirement
`touchUpdatedAt`'s monotonic/idempotent guard (`updatedAt: { lt: at }`) is untested

Existing controller unit test still stubs the removed `getSummaries` dependency instead of `getEditors`
A database failure in `touchUpdatedAt` escapes as a 500, contradicting the controller's stated "always 200 so Yorkie won't retry" contract

Issue outcome only half-delivered in-repo: the webhook is never registered by anything in the change

Presentation consumers of raw boolean values were not widened alongside isCheckboxChecked: `defaultAlign` centers only the exact `TRUE`/`FALSE` strings, so a lowercase/mixed-case value that now renders as a checked checkbox is still classified as plain left-aligned text everywhere the checkbox glyph is not drawn (e.g. after `removeCheckbox`, which deliberately leaves the value behind).
Case-folded checkbox rendering can make displayed state diverge from the stored literal (UI state spoofing for approval-style checkboxes)

Widened checkbox matching now disagrees with the formula engine for mixed-case booleans: a cell holding `True` renders CHECKED (isCheckboxChecked case-folds) but `Evaluator.resolveValue` only coerces the exact strings `'TRUE'`/`'true'` to a boolean, so formulas referencing that cell see a plain string. A checked box and `=IF(A1,...)`/`=COUNTIF(range,TRUE)` therefore report opposite states for the same cell.
Space over a formula-backed checkbox is now silently swallowed (preventDefault with no action and no feedback)
No test exercises the click/Space view paths that reach the new formula guard
Fix applied at the compare/render layer rather than at ingestion, leaving other consumers of the raw value inconsistent
Remove the duplicate empty `Review` section.
Read-then-write in toggleCheckboxAt is not atomic; two rapid toggles can interleave and lose one flip

Task file has two '## Review' sections; the second is a leftover template placeholder ('(filled after implementation)') that was never removed even though the earlier '## Review' section already contains the filled-in content.

The new doc comment (and the design doc) justify the change by asserting the formula engine already treats TRUE/FALSE case-insensitively; it does not — it accepts only the two exact spellings `TRUE`/`true`. The comment describes a contract other modules do not implement, which will mislead the next reader/maintainer of this helper.
Mark the old scope note as superseded.

The formula guard makes both view entry points silently swallow the interaction: the Space handler calls `event.preventDefault()` before `toggleCheckboxAt` and only re-renders on `true`, and the click handler calls `preventDefault()`/`return` regardless of the result. Over a formula-backed checkbox the user now gets no toggle and no feedback, and the keystroke/click is consumed rather than falling through to normal editing/selection.
New `value.toUpperCase()` fallback runs on unbounded, attacker-supplied cell text on the per-repaint render path (client-side memory-churn DoS)
toggleCheckboxAt still returns `true` on paths where setData silently writes nothing (spill ghost cells, pivot sheets)
Formula-guard test's "writes no literal" claim is not asserted (cell.v never checked)
Design-scope widened vs the task's literal criterion (both custom values absent, not just checkedValue)

The new case-fold gate tests `checkedValue === undefined && uncheckedValue === undefined` with strict equality, while `checkedValueOf`/`uncheckedValueOf` normalize with `??`. A rule that round-trips through JSON/Yorkie or an external REST payload carrying `checkedValue: null` (or `''`) is treated as "has custom values" by the gate but as default by the accessors, so the case-insensitive branch silently switches off (with `''` it also matches nothing). Would need to confirm whether the Yorkie/REST layer can persist null/empty here.
Case-fold gate uses strict `=== undefined` while checkedValueOf/uncheckedValueOf use `??`, so `null` (or `''`) custom values behave inconsistently
